images.text: Amy: Today's workshop is going to focus on leadership. We have to enhance our creativity and open up to the possibility of becoming effective leaders. That is to say, we will take a closer look at becoming assertive and communicating more fluidly. In order to have credibility as leaders, we have to first know what our motivations are. Second, we must create a vision for the future. Third, we have to communicate that vision in a way that inspires others. Motivation and inspiration are the first things to identity. I want everyone to try to define what motivates them to live, breathe and succeed. So let's start with you, Will.

Will: As far as I'm concerned, love is a huge motivator. To be more precise, being loved is a motivator. I mean, I would say that I'm the type of person who needs to be loved. I'm sure most of us do ... and money is another huge incentive. Am I on the right track?
Amy: Definitely.

Vanessa: When I was at school, I realized I was driven by the idea of getting rewards and praise. Now, I think that is a bit negative.
Amy: Not necessarily. To be honest, many of us feel that way. We are social animals who need to be part of a pack, after all. The approval of others is very important, but it must not be to the detriment of one's own moral fiber.
Vanessa: I agree with you there. To my mind, if your values are not solid and ethical, you could be in trouble.

Expressing Your Position In Different Situations
You use discourse markers to express your position and to show how ideas are connected. You use different discourse markers for different situations.

Discourse markers can show a connection to what you want to say and what was said before. They can also show your position and opinion on a particular situation.

When writing, you use a comma after the discourse marker.

You use the modals must and have (got) to to express necessity in the present.
You use the negative forms of the modals need to and have to to express absence of necessity in the present.
Must refers to a necessary condition that comes from the subject and may be directed at the subject or the person the subject is talking to or about. It is used to express a strong necessity.

Example:
    We must create a vision for the future.

Have (got) to expresses external obligations, which come from outside of the subject. These may be rules and regulations over which the subject has no control. It is used to express necessity in a lower degree than with must.

Example:
    We have to make some changes.
Absence of necessity is expressed with the negative form of have to, not with mustn't.

Example:
    You don't have to own everything in life to be happy.
